topic: Diabetes care processes in primary care

audits.title: Improving organisational systems for diabetes care in Australian Indigenous communities.

cycle1.result: Baseline: 6-monthly HbA1c 41%, 3-monthly BP 63%, annual cholesterol 56%, biennial eye check 34%, 3-monthly foot check 20%; mean HbA1c 9.3%.

audits.intervention: Two annual cycles of assessment, feedback workshops, action planning and system changes.

cycle2.result: HbA1c testing 74%, BP 76%, cholesterol 74%, eye check 54%, foot check 58%; mean HbA1c 8.9%.

audits.other_findings: Medication adjustment after high HbA1c rose from 10% to 24% at year 1 but was not maintained at year 2; no BP or cholesterol improvement.
audits.citation: Bailie R, Si D, Dowden M, O'Donoghue L, Connors C, Robinson G, et al.. Improving organisational systems for diabetes care in Australian Indigenous communities. BMC Health Serv Res. 2007;7:67. doi:10.1186/1472-6963-7-67. PMID: 17480239.

audits.title: Impacts and outcomes of diabetes care in a high risk remote Indigenous community over time: implications for practice.
audits.standard: National optimal diabetes management guidelines (regular monitoring of care processes)
audits.setting: Remote Indigenous community primary care service, Queensland

cycle1.result: Earlier audit of diabetes care processes and outcomes (figures not given in abstract).

cycle2.result: Recording of diabetic care processes decreased by between 5 and 32% compared with 2004; intermediate clinical measures stable or poorer except total cholesterol.

audits.other_findings: Improvements reported from 1999 to 2003 were not sustained; no intervention between audits described.
audits.citation: Forbes MP, Ling J, Jones S, McDermott R. Impacts and outcomes of diabetes care in a high risk remote Indigenous community over time: implications for practice. Aust J Prim Health. 2013;19(2):107-112. doi:10.1071/py11144. PMID: 22950855.

audits.title: Clinical audit of diabetes management can improve the quality of care in a resource-limited primary care setting.
audits.setting: Primary health-care facilities, Metro health district, Western Cape

cycle1.result: Baseline medians for six of nine processes were below 50%.

audits.intervention: Clinical audit and feedback, with co-interventions after the baseline audit

cycle2.result: Statistically significant improvement in seven of nine clinical processes (annual audits 2005, 2007, 2008 and 2009).

audits.other_findings: Number of participating community health centres fell from 40 to 30; management and government support contributed.
audits.citation: Govender I, Ehrlich R, Van Vuuren U, De Vries E, Namane M, De Sa A, et al.. Clinical audit of diabetes management can improve the quality of care in a resource-limited primary care setting. Int J Qual Health Care. 2012;24(6):612-618. doi:10.1093/intqhc/mzs063. PMID: 23118094.

audits.title: Results of a mixed-methods evaluation of partnerships for health: a quality improvement initiative for diabetes care.
audits.standard: Diabetes clinical process and outcome targets (e.g. LDL, blood pressure, A1c)
audits.setting: Primary care practices in Southwestern Ontario (Partnerships for Health programme)

cycle1.result: Before audit of 30 charts per physician (35 physicians); baseline figures not given in abstract.

audits.intervention: Partnerships for Health quality improvement programme: team approach, better tracking of patient data and increased patient involvement.

cycle2.result: Significant improvement (P ≤ .005) in documented A1c, cholesterol, ACR, creatinine, eGFR, ECG, foot/eye/neuropathy examination, BMI, waist circumference and depression screening; more patients at LDL and BP targets (P ≤ .001).

audits.other_findings: Mean A1c fell significantly in patients above target at baseline.
audits.citation: Harris S, Paquette-Warren J, Roberts S, Fournie M, Thind A, Ryan BL, et al.. Results of a mixed-methods evaluation of partnerships for health: a quality improvement initiative for diabetes care. J Am Board Fam Med. 2013;26(6):711-719. doi:10.3122/jabfm.2013.06.120211. PMID: 24204067.

audits.title: Quality improvement in practice: improving diabetes care and patient outcomes in Aboriginal Community Controlled Health Services.
audits.standard: Diabetes care activities and clinical targets (HbA1c)
audits.setting: Four Aboriginal Community Controlled Health Services, Kimberley, Western Australia

cycle1.result: In three of four services at least 71% had cholesterol, 89% BP and 84% HbA1c recorded; 31% met HbA1c target at DAHS vs 16% at ACCHS-3.

audits.other_findings: Effective features: defined staff roles, Aboriginal Health Workers, recall systems and local ownership of CQI.
audits.citation: Stoneman A, Atkinson D, Davey M, Marley JV. Quality improvement in practice: improving diabetes care and patient outcomes in Aboriginal Community Controlled Health Services. BMC Health Serv Res. 2014;14:481. doi:10.1186/1472-6963-14-481. PMID: 25288282.

audits.title: Does audit improve diabetes care in a primary care setting? A management tool to address health system gaps.
audits.standard: Standard guidelines for monitoring blood pressure, blood glucose, lipid profile and renal function
audits.setting: Non-communicable disease clinic, rural health and training centre, Puducherry

cycle1.result: BP 78 (50%), blood glucose 70 (44.9%), lipid profile 49 (31.4%), renal function 19 (12.2%).

audits.intervention: Clinical audit cycle applied (details not reported).

cycle2.result: Monitoring improved significantly: blood glucose by 35%, BP by 20.7%, lipid profile by 36.4% and renal function by 56.1%.

audits.citation: Pruthu TK, Majella MG, Nair D, Ramaswamy G, Palanivel C, Subitha L, et al.. Does audit improve diabetes care in a primary care setting? A management tool to address health system gaps. J Nat Sci Biol Med. 2015;6(Suppl 1):S58-62. doi:10.4103/0976-9668.166087. PMID: 26604621.

audits.title: Emerging standards for diabetes care from a city-wide primary care audit.
audits.standard: Peer group standards of mean performance and of excellence derived from aggregated practice data
audits.setting: Manchester practices in the Diabetes 2000 project (city-wide primary care audit)

cycle1.result: Checks in preceding year: HbA1c 56.8%, weight or BMI 67.8%, foot pulses 37.3%, ankle reflexes 31.3%, proteinuria 60%, fundoscopy 48.2%, blood pressure 81.1%, cholesterol or lipids 34%.

audits.intervention: Standards fed back to practices so they could compare with the city mean and best performers and set their own targets.
audits.other_findings: Best practices examined 79% of fundi, 84% of foot pulses, 74% of ankle reflexes and gave smoking advice in 65%. Referral in preceding year: specialist nurse 14.4%, optician or ophthalmologist 22.1%, chiropodist 25%, dietitian 21.5%.
audits.citation: Benett IJ, Lambert C, Hinds G, Kirton C. Emerging standards for diabetes care from a city-wide primary care audit. Diabet Med. 1994;11(5):489-492. doi:10.1111/j.1464-5491.1994.tb00312.x. PMID: 8088129.

audits.title: Diabetes care in general practice: an approach to audit of process and outcome.
audits.standard: Published protocols for diabetes care processes
audits.setting: Four general practices with organised diabetes care, Newcastle upon Tyne

cycle1.result: Recommended processes completed in a high percentage of patients; adverse outcomes limited and metabolic measures not unsatisfactory.

audits.other_findings: Data collected at minimal cost where structured records were completed.
audits.citation: Tunbridge FK, Millar JP, Schofield PJ, Spencer JA, Young G, Home PD. Diabetes care in general practice: an approach to audit of process and outcome. Br J Gen Pract. 1993;43(372):291-295. PMID: 8398246.
